chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Amr ibn Jumay', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most superior of the people is the one who has passion for worship, so he embraces it, loves it with his heart, and engages with it with his body, and devotes himself to it; thus, he does not care whether he experiences ease or hardship in the world.'

key_terms.بَاشَرَهَا: He engaged with it / touched it (physically or practically)
key_terms.تَفَرَّغَ: He devoted himself / freed himself for it
key_terms.عَشِقَ: To have a deep passion or love for something
key_terms.فَعَانَقَهَا: He embraced it (metaphorically holding it close)

ai.seo_question: What is the most superior quality of a person in worship according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni narrates this hadith to define the pinnacle of spiritual status as one who 'kisses' and 'embraces' worship with total bodily and heartful immersion, rendering worldly conditions of ease or hardship irrelevant. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) and the transformation of ritual acts into a state of continuous spiritual joy, where the worshipper finds contentment in the act itself rather than external outcomes.
